summary_en: Six hand-drawn SVG weather icons on one consistent grid with seamless looping animations, pause and size controls, and reduced-motion support.
summary_ar: ست أيقونات طقس SVG مرسومة يدويًا على شبكة موحّدة، بحركات متكررة بلا انقطاع، مع أزرار للإيقاف وتغيير الحجم ودعم تفضيل تقليل الحركة.
prompt:
Design and animate a set of six weather icons as inline SVG — the kind of polished, looping micro-animations a premium weather app would ship.

Icons, in this order, each in a card with a caption and a short forecast line (e.g. "Clear · 24°"): Clear, Partly cloudy, Rain, Snow, Thunderstorm, Wind.

1. Each icon is an inline <svg class="wx-icon" role="img" viewBox="0 0 64 64"> containing a <title> with its name. Write the six SVGs directly in the HTML (not generated by script).
2. One consistent drawing system across all six: 64-unit grid, 2-unit strokes with round caps and joins, one shared cloud shape, and colours from CSS custom properties / currentColor so the set works on light and dark backgrounds.
3. Animations — each loops seamlessly with no visible jump at the loop point; durations between 2 and 6 s:
   - Clear: rays rotate slowly and pulse.
   - Partly cloudy: the cloud drifts gently in front of the sun.
   - Rain: drops fall from the cloud in a staggered rhythm, fading as they fall.
   - Snow: flakes drift down while swaying from side to side.
   - Thunderstorm: the bolt flashes at irregular-feeling intervals (e.g. a double flash every ~3 s) with a subtle cloud flicker.
   - Wind: streamlines draw on and off along their paths (stroke-dashoffset).
   Use CSS keyframes, SMIL or the Web Animations API — no animation libraries and no canvas.
4. Controls: a button id="motion-toggle" (aria-pressed) that pauses and resumes every animation, and an <input type="range" id="icon-size"> (32–160 px) that resizes all icons live. A light/dark theme switch is a welcome extra.
5. Respect prefers-reduced-motion: show calm static poses (or barely perceptible motion) to users who ask for reduced motion.
6. Layout: a responsive grid of cards — 3 columns on desktop, 2 on mobile.

Every id named in this brief must exist in the initial HTML markup (fill or update those elements with JavaScript if you like).

Delivery rules (hard requirements)
- Return ONE complete HTML document (<!doctype html> … </html>) with all CSS and JavaScript inline, in a single ```html code block.
- No external resources at all: no CDNs, web fonts, remote images, iframes or network requests. Use system font stacks, inline SVG, CSS and canvas.
- The page runs inside a sandboxed iframe with an opaque origin: localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies and alert/confirm/prompt are unavailable, and form submission is blocked (the submit event never fires). Do not depend on them: wrap any storage access in try/catch, drive forms with type="button" click handlers and handle the Enter key yourself.
- No errors in the browser console. Include <html lang="en"> and a viewport meta tag.
- It must work at 1280×800 and at 390×844: no horizontal page scrolling at 390 px, comfortable touch targets.

rubric.guide: Six icons that clearly belong to one family: same grid, stroke weight, corner language and shared cloud; balanced optical sizes; readable at 32 px and crisp at 160 px; colours work on light and dark.

Each motion fits its weather and loops seamlessly (no jumps), easing and staggering feel natural, the storm flash has rhythm, wind lines draw on/off cleanly without stray caps or dots. Mechanical linear motion everywhere = 4-5.
Pause really stops everything (and resumes in place), size slider works live, role="img" + title on every icon, reduced-motion respected, visible focus.

Readable, well-structured code: data and configuration defined once, small named functions, no dead code or copy-pasted blocks, sensible event handling and cleanup. Shared symbols / CSS variables instead of copy-pasted paths and colours. 9-10: a senior engineer would merge it as is; 5-6: works but tangled or repetitive; 0-3: unreadable or hacky.

summary_en: A choreographed 6-second logo reveal (stroke draw, gradient fill, staggered letters, tagline, settle) with exact scrubbing, replay, pause and speed control.
summary_ar: عرض افتتاحي متقن للشعار خلال 6 ثوانٍ (رسم الخطوط، وتعبئة متدرجة، وحروف متتابعة، وشعار نصي، واستقرار) مع تمرير دقيق على الخط الزمني وإعادة التشغيل والإيقاف والتحكم بالسرعة.
prompt:
Create the 6-second intro animation for "Kestrel Maps", a (fictional) mapping start-up — a brand reveal for its launch page — together with timeline controls.

Brand: a geometric kestrel/compass mark that you design as an SVG path, the wordmark "KESTREL" and the tagline "Maps that know the terrain".

Choreography (timings ±150 ms):
1. 0.0–1.6 s: the mark's outline draws itself (stroke-dashoffset or equivalent).
2. 1.2–2.2 s: the mark fills with a gradient while the outline fades.
3. 2.0–3.4 s: the letters of "KESTREL" rise and fade in one after another with a 60 ms stagger — each letter is its own element with class="letter".
4. 3.2–4.2 s: the tagline slides/fades in.
5. 4.2–6.0 s: settle — the background gradient shifts and a topographic contour-line pattern sweeps in behind the logo.
After 6 s the final composition holds with a subtle ambient loop (e.g. slowly drifting contour lines) so the page never looks frozen.

Timeline controls
- A button id="replay" restarts from 0.
- A button id="play-pause" (aria-pressed) pauses and resumes.
- An <input type="range" id="scrubber"> (0–6000 ms) scrubs the timeline: dragging it pauses playback and renders the exact frame for that time; while playing, the scrubber follows the playhead.
- An element id="time" shows the current time like "2.40 s".
- A <select id="speed"> offers 0.5×, 1× and 2× playback.
Use deliberate easing (no linear motion except continuous loops), overlapping actions and a clear hierarchy. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by showing the final composition immediately with only a short fade. It must look right at 390 px (logo scales down, controls wrap) and at 1280 px.

Do not depend on them: wrap any storage access in try/catch, drive forms with type="button" click handlers and handle the Enter key yourself.
- No errors in the browser console. Include <html lang="en"> and a viewport meta tag.
- It must work at 1280×800 and at 390×844: no horizontal page scrolling at 390 px, comfortable touch targets.

rubric.guide: Beats land on the specified timings with overlapping actions, purposeful easing (anticipation/overshoot where it helps), a readable hierarchy (mark → wordmark → tagline → settle) and a calm ambient loop afterwards. Everything-at-once or linear tweens score ≤ 4.
Scrubbing renders the exact frame for any time (forwards and backwards), the scrubber follows playback, replay/pause/speed work in any order, time readout accurate to the frame.
A distinctive, well-constructed mark, good typography and spacing for the wordmark and tagline, tasteful colour and background.
Reduced motion honoured, controls labelled and keyboard-operable, responsive at 390 px.

summary_ar: أربعة عناصر واجهة تتحرك بمحرك نوابض مخمّدة مكتوب يدويًا: مفتاح قابل للمقاطعة، وزر إعجاب بانفجار جسيمات وعدّاد دوّار، ومبدّل مقاطع نابض، ومكدّس إشعارات يُسحب للإغلاق.
prompt:
Build a small gallery of four UI micro-interactions animated with real spring physics — the tactile feel of a top-tier mobile app.

Write your own damped-spring integrator in JavaScript (stiffness, damping, mass; integrated per frame with a fixed or clamped timestep) and drive these with it — not CSS transitions:
1. Toggle: a button id="toggle-demo" with role="switch" and aria-checked. The knob springs to the other side with a slight overshoot and squishes (stretches) while pressed.
2. Like: a button id="like-btn" (aria-pressed) with a heart and the count 1,284. Liking pops the heart (a velocity kick into a spring), fires a burst of 8–12 particles and rolls the counter to 1,285 with digits sliding vertically like an odometer; unliking returns to 1,284. Keep the number available as text for screen readers.
3. Segmented control: Day / Week / Month in a container id="segmented" with role="radiogroup" (options role="radio", aria-checked, roving tabindex). A sliding indicator springs to the selected option, adapting its width; Arrow keys move the selection.
4. Notification stack: a button id="notify" adds a notification card that springs in from below; at most 3 cards are visible, older ones scale down and tuck behind like a stack; the front card can be swiped/dragged horizontally (pointer events) — released with enough velocity or distance it flings away, otherwise it springs back; cards auto-dismiss after 5 s.
Every animation must be interruptible: clicking again mid-flight retargets from the current position and velocity (no jumps, no restarting from rest).
Respect prefers-reduced-motion (instant state changes, no particle burst). Lay the four demos out as cards in a grid (2 × 2 on desktop, stacked on mobile).

Squish on press, fling velocity measured from pointer samples, swipe threshold sensible, stack depth/scale correct, auto-dismiss, keyboard support in the segmented control.

switch/radiogroup roles with states, readable like count, reduced motion honoured, focus visible.

summary_en: A schematic transit map with trains moving on a computed timetable, eased station dwells, next-arrival predictions per station, line filters and pan/zoom.
summary_ar: خريطة نقل تخطيطية تتحرك فيها القطارات وفق جدول زمني محسوب، مع توقف سلس في المحطات، وتوقّع للقطارات القادمة لكل محطة، وتصفية للخطوط، وتحريك وتكبير.
prompt:
Build a live, animated schematic map of the (fictional) Port Avalon Metro.

Network (coordinates in a 1000 × 640 design space; stations in order):
- Red — Harbour Line: Westmere (80,320) · Foundry Lane (180,320) · Cathedral (300,320) · Market Square (420,320) · Central (540,320) · Opera (660,320) · Harbourfront (780,200) · Lighthouse (900,200)
- Blue — Hill Line: Northgate (300,60) · Observatory (300,180) · Cathedral (300,320) · Tannery (300,440) · Old Mill (180,560) · Westfield (80,560)
- Green — River Line: Kingsbridge (540,60) · Museum (540,180) · Central (540,320) · Riverside (540,440) · Southpark (660,560) · Airport (860,560)
Cathedral and Central are interchanges (18 unique stations).

Timetable (simulated time): trains shuttle end to end and back. Between adjacent stations a train takes 2 min (easing in and out), it dwells 30 s at every intermediate station and lays over 1 min at each terminus. Red runs 3 trains, Blue 2, Green 2, evenly spaced around the round trip; at 06:00 train 1 of each line is departing its first-listed terminus. The simulated clock starts at 06:00 and runs at 1 simulated minute per real second.

Requirements
1. Draw the map as inline SVG scaled to the viewport: thick coloured routes with rounded joins, a station marker for each unique station — one element with class="station" per station (18) — interchanges drawn distinctly (e.g. a white capsule/ring), and clear labels that do not sit on top of the routes.
2. Trains: one element with class="train" per train (7), each in its line colour, positioned along the route according to the timetable, pointing in its direction of travel.
3. Clock: an element id="clock" showing the simulated time as HH:MM.
4. Legend: one button per line with class="line-toggle" (aria-pressed) that hides/shows that line and its trains.
5. Station info: hovering, focusing (Tab) or tapping a station shows a panel id="tooltip" with the station name and, for every visible line serving it, the next two arrival times (HH:MM) and the direction ("→ Lighthouse") — computed from the timetable, not random.
6. Pan by dragging and zoom with the wheel/pinch and with + / − buttons, by changing the SVG viewBox (within sensible limits).
7. Stations are keyboard-focusable with an accessible name. With prefers-reduced-motion, trains jump between stations instead of gliding.
8. Smooth at 60 fps (no layout thrashing) and usable at 390 px (map fits, panel docked at the bottom).

- The page runs inside a sandboxed iframe with an opaque origin: localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies and alert/confirm/prompt are unavailable, and form submission is blocked (the submit event never fires). Do not depend on them: wrap any storage access in try/catch, drive forms with type="button" click handlers and handle the Enter key yourself.
- No errors in the browser console. Include <html lang="en"> and a viewport meta tag.
- It must work at 1280×800 and at 390×844: no horizontal page scrolling at 390 px, comfortable touch targets.

rubric.guide: Clean schematic: consistent line weights, octilinear routes with rounded joins, readable non-overlapping labels, distinct interchanges, tasteful legend and colours; looks like a real transit authority map.

Trains follow the specified timetable exactly (2-min eased runs, 30-s dwells, 1-min terminus layovers, even spacing, correct start positions), turn around at termini, point in their travel direction; arrival predictions match the train positions.
Tooltip on hover/focus/tap with next two arrivals per line, line toggles also hide trains and update the panel, pan/zoom smooth and bounded on mouse and touch.
Single rAF loop updating transforms only, keyboard-focusable stations with names, reduced motion honoured.

summary_en: A hierarchical SVG robot with a procedural walk/jog cycle: no foot sliding, hip bob, counter-swinging arms, follow-through, jump with squash & stretch, and parallax scenery.
summary_ar: روبوت SVG بهيكل هرمي ودورة مشي وهرولة إجرائية: دون انزلاق للقدمين، مع اهتزاز الورك، وتأرجح الذراعين المعاكس، والحركة الثانوية المتأخرة، والقفز بالانضغاط والتمدد، وخلفية متعددة الطبقات بتأثير المنظور.
prompt:
Animate a character walk cycle in SVG + JavaScript: "Pip", a small (fictional) courier robot, walking through a parallax landscape.

Character: build it from SVG shapes inside <svg id="scene">; the character is a group with id="character" containing a torso with a satchel, a head with a visor and an antenna, two arms (upper arm + forearm) and two legs (thigh + shin + foot), all as nested <g> groups rotated at their joints — a real hierarchy, not independent floating pieces.

Animation requirements
1. A proper walk cycle with contact, down, passing and up poses; the hips bob (lowest at the down pose), the arms counter-swing to the legs, and a slight forward lean grows with speed.
2. No foot sliding: while a foot is planted it stays fixed relative to the ground layer (use inverse kinematics, or match the ground scroll speed exactly to the stride).
3. Secondary motion: the antenna and the satchel follow through with lag and settle with damping.
4. Parallax: at least 3 background layers (far, mid, ground) scrolling seamlessly at different rates proportional to the walking speed; the ground layer moves at the planted foot's speed.
5. Speed: <input type="range" id="speed"> from 0 to 2 (default 1): 0 = idle (breathing, blinking, nothing scrolls), 1 = walk, 2 = brisk jog with longer strides and more lean; changes blend smoothly with no popping. ArrowRight/ArrowLeft change the speed by 0.1.
6. Jump: Space and a button id="jump" make Pip jump with anticipation (crouch), squash & stretch, an airborne pose and a landing squash; pressing again while airborne does nothing.
7. Time-based animation with requestAnimationFrame (frame-rate independent). With prefers-reduced-motion, start idle.
8. The scene scales to the viewport (viewBox) and works at 390 × 844 with on-screen controls.

Every id named in this brief must exist in the initial HTML markup (fill or update those elements with JavaScript if you like).

Delivery rules (hard requirements)
- Return ONE complete HTML document (<!doctype html> … </html>) with all CSS and JavaScript inline, in a single ```html code block.
- No external resources at all: no CDNs, web fonts, remote images, iframes or network requests. Use system font stacks, inline SVG, CSS and canvas.
- The page runs inside a sandboxed iframe with an opaque origin: localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies and alert/confirm/prompt are unavailable, and form submission is blocked (the submit event never fires). Do not depend on them: wrap any storage access in try/catch, drive forms with type="button" click handlers and handle the Enter key yourself.
- No errors in the browser console. Include <html lang="en"> and a viewport meta tag.
- It must work at 1280×800 and at 390×844: no horizontal page scrolling at 390 px, comfortable touch targets.

rubric.guide: Convincing weight shift and hip bob, arcs in the swing foot, counter-swinging arms, overlapping action on antenna/satchel, anticipation and squash & stretch on the jump, smooth speed blending. Any visible foot sliding or limbs detaching caps this at 4.
Appealing, readable robot with clear silhouette and proportions; joints placed where the hierarchy rotates; consistent style.
Three or more seamless layers with depth-correct speeds, ground locked to the feet, pleasant palette; idle state stops scrolling.
Slider, arrow keys and jump (key + button) behave as specified on desktop and touch.

Pose computed from a phase variable (and IK) with clear functions; no frame-count-based timing. 9-10: a senior engineer would merge it as is; 5-6: works but tangled or repetitive; 0-3: unreadable or hacky.
